title: The catacombs and the fish
hookLine: the Greek word for fish spells Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior

cards: Two curved lines, crossing at one end to make a tail. It's on the backs of cars, on necklaces, on the sign of a plumber who wants you to know something about him.

Now go underground, into the tunnels outside the walls of ancient Rome, where Christians buried their dead. On the plaster, by lamplight, the same creature shows up: a fish, sometimes swimming beside a basket of bread.
Today's word is that fish, and it's hiding a sentence.

teach.b: The Greek word for fish is ichthys. Spell it in Greek capitals and each letter starts a word: Iesous, Jesus. Christos, Christ.
Theou, of God. Huios, Son. Soter, Savior.
A whole creed, folded into one small animal. Saint Augustine explained it in The City of God, so by his time the word game was known. Second, why a fish fit so well.
The Gospels are full of them.
Jesus calls fishermen from their boats, in the Douay-Rheims: "Come ye after me, and I will make you to be fishers of men." He feeds a crowd with loaves and a few fish. Third, the water.

The writer Tertullian called Christians little fishes, born in water after the example of their Fish, Jesus Christ. He meant baptism: born in water, and like fish, kept alive by staying in it. Fourth, the catacombs.
Films sometimes show Christians living down there in hiding.

They were cemeteries: long tunnels of graves, where families came to bury and to pray, and where painters put their hope on the walls. Some read the fish beside the bread as a picture of the Eucharist.

teach.h: JESUS CHRIST, SON OF GOD, SAVIOR.
teach.b: A story people tell says one Christian would draw half a fish in the dirt, and a stranger who finished it was a friend. That story is hard to trace to any early writer.
But the fish did work as a secret sign in a deeper way. To an outsider, it was only a fish. To someone who knew the letters, it was a confession of faith, hidden in plain sight.

how: Some Catholics wear or display the fish as a sign of faith, and the early Christian paintings of fish and bread in the Roman catacombs can still be visited today.

games.q: you're a fisherman casting a net into the lake. a teacher walks along the shore and says: come after me. what do you do?
o: leave the nets and follow him.
ask him to come back tomorrow.
games.why: Matthew says they left their nets at once and followed him. the fishermen became fishers of men.

practice: Draw a small fish, on paper or with a fingertip on your palm: two curved lines, crossing at the tail. Then go through the five words slowly, one for each breath: Jesus, Christ, Son, of God, Savior.
If you pray, let the words be your prayer; if you're learning, just notice how much one little drawing was made to hold.

wordCard.voice: Ichthys. Greek for fish, and a sign whose letters spell Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior. Today's word.
